scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a router reload on r4, OSPF routes for the 18.x.x.x
loopbacks (r8's loopback range) and 80.0.0.0/8 (Area 2)
disappeared from r1's routing table. r1 still has routes
for Area 0 and Area 1. r4 reports Area 1 is healthy.
Investigate.

injection.action: remove the area 1 virtual-link to r8

post_inject_check.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf interface vlink0" 2>&1 | grep -c "Interface"

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r4 OSPF virtual-link to r8 (router-id 18.1.4.1)
Mechanism: r8 is the ABR for Area 2 (which contains the 80.0.0.0/8
  network and r8's 18.x loopbacks). Area 2 is not directly attached
  to Area 0 (the backbone) — it touches Area 1 via r4 and Area 1
  to Area 0 via r3/r5. OSPF requires every non-backbone area to
  have either a direct connection to Area 0 or a virtual-link
  through a transit area. r4 provides that virtual-link for Area 2
  via Area 1 (transit) to r8 (router-id 18.1.4.1). With the
  virtual-link removed, r8 cannot inject Area 2 LSAs into the
  backbone, and the rest of the network loses all routes for
  Area 2 prefixes.
Localization: r4 (and r8, which is the other endpoint, but the
  primary configuration change is on r4)
Root cause: Area 1 virtual-link 18.1.4.1 missing on r4
Fix: `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "area 1 virtual-link 18.1.4.1"`
  on r4

line.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf interface vlink0" 2>&1 | grep -c "Interface"

agent.diagnosis_text:
r8 is an OSPF ABR connecting Area 2 (its 18.x.x.x loopbacks and the
80.0.0.0/8 stub) to the rest of the network. Because Area 2 is not
physically connected to the backbone (Area 0), r8 uses an OSPF virtual
link traversing Area 1 to reach the backbone. The virtual link is
defined in r8's configuration as "area 1 virtual-link 14.1.4.1", where
14.1.4.1 is r4's router-id. r4 acts as the far-end transit ABR for this
virtual link: it sits in both Area 0 and Area 1, so the virtual link
passes through Area 1 (the transit area) and "exits" at r4 into Area 0.

After r4's reload, its ospfd configuration was loaded from the startup
file, which is missing the matching endpoint statement: "area 1
virtual-link 18.1.4.1" (r8's router-id). Without that statement, r4
does not participate in the virtual link. As a result, r8's Area 0
interface shows zero adjacent neighbors (confirmed by "show ip ospf" on
r8) and r4's Area 1 shows zero virtual adjacencies. Area 2's inter-area
LSAs are never injected into the backbone, so no router in Area 0 or
Area 1 — including r1 — learns the 18.x.x.x routes or the 80.0.0.0/8
prefix. Area 1 itself remains fully healthy because all physical
adjacencies (r4-r5, r4-r6, r4-r3) were unaffected by the reload.

Root cause: r4's startup configuration is missing "area 1 virtual-link
18.1.4.1", so the OSPF virtual link that connects Area 2 to the backbone
has no functional far-end endpoint after r4 reloaded.

Corrective fix: Add "area 1 virtual-link 18.1.4.1" under "router ospf"
on r4 (and persist it to /etc/frr/frr.conf). The virtual link will
re-establish, r8's backbone adjacency will come up, Area 2 summary LSAs
will flood into Area 0/1, and r1 will re-learn all 18.x.x.x and
80.0.0.0/8 routes within one OSPF SPF cycle.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names r4 as the far-end transit ABR and the device whose startup config is missing the 'area 1 virtual-link 18.1.4.1' statement.
The report explicitly names the OSPF virtual-link (area 1 virtual-link) and states the missing "area 1 virtual-link 18.1.4.1" on r4 as the root cause.
Agent explicitly names Area 2 and states the affected prefixes (18.x loopbacks and 80.0.0.0/8).
The writeup explicitly explains that Area 1 is the transit area for the virtual link—showing how it traverses Area 1 and exits at r4 into Area 0—clearly describing the transit-area mechanism.
Correctly instructs adding the missing 'area 1 virtual-link 18.1.4.1' under router ospf on r4 and persisting it, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's logs show r4's running-config lacking the virtual-link and indicate r8 is configured with a virtual-link to r4; the conclusion that the missing reciprocal virtual-link on r4 broke the Area 2-to-backbone path follows logically and the investigation covered the relevant devices.
